🧠 Crypto News Brief: Crypto starts November in recovery mode: Binance reopened withdrawals after its record $6.3B hack and bitcoin is steadying near $78K, but heavy ETF outflows and fresh wallet drains keep sentiment fragile ahead of the U.S. midterms. 🏦 Binance Reopens Withdrawals: $3.64B Net Outflow, 95% of Hack Losses Covered Binance restored withdrawals in phases from 06:00 UTC on Sunday, three days after hackers the FBI links to North Korea drained about $6.3 billion from its hot wallets. In the first 9.5 hours, users withdrew $4.65 billion against $1.01 billion in deposits, a net outflow of roughly $3.64 billion, or 2.1% of the exchange's $171 billion in assets. Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen funds from its own reserves, while remaining networks are still being restored. Read full story 📉 Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $643M, Turning October Red After Binance Hack U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $643 million on Friday, the first trading session after the Binance breach, snapping a four-day inflow streak. BlackRock's IBIT ($234M) and Fidelity's FBTC ($201M) led redemptions, leaving October with $515 million in net outflows, the first negative month since June. Spot ether ETFs fared worse, posting a record $1.61 billion monthly outflow. More details 🗳️ Bitcoin Steadies Near $78K as U.S. Midterms and Jobs Data Loom Bitcoin is holding around $78,000 on Monday after a bruising October, as Binance's withdrawal restart eases contagion fears. Traders now face Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections and Friday's October jobs report, with rate decisions from the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Bank of England also on deck. Kenya's grace period for existing crypto firms ends Wednesday, and Zcash's NU7 upgrade is expected Thursday. See the week ahead 🇨🇳 China's Communist Party Puts Crypto on Its Anti-Corruption Hit List A resolution adopted at the Central Committee's Fifth Plenary Session, published in full by Xinhua on November 1, orders investigators to crack down on corruption carried out through the internet, virtual currency, cross-border funds and blockchain. The document targets crypto as a tool for hiding bribes and moving illicit money; it does not name bitcoin or address trading, mining or stablecoins, and China's 2021 crypto ban stays as is.
